apiCenter.title: API Center
apiCenter.subtitle: Pull CryptoGuide data into your own tools with the REST API and webhooks. Whale plan only.
apiCenter.terms: All data served by the API is informational only and is not investment advice. Redistribution, resale, or public re-publication is prohibited; every response carries the same terms in its meta field.
apiCenter.secretOnce: This value is shown only once. Store it somewhere safe.
apiCenter.webhookSigning: Every webhook request includes an x-cryptoguide-signature header (HMAC-SHA256). Verify it with the secret issued at registration.

docs.intro: Three read-only JSON endpoints under /api/v1, one key per request, and signed webhooks for new briefs and reports. Everything below matches the running code.

auth.title: Authentication
auth.body: Send your key in an Authorization: Bearer header or in x-api-key. Keys start with cg_live_, are shown once when issued, and can be revoked here at any time. Up to 5 active keys per account. A key stops working the moment the Whale subscription lapses and is also subject to the regional availability of the API.

envelope.title: Response shape
envelope.body: Every successful response is a JSON object with a data field and a meta field. Market endpoints add stale and updatedAt. stale: true means every upstream source failed and you are seeing our last good value; updatedAt is when that value was fetched. data is null only if we have never had a value for that endpoint (or, for briefs, if nothing has been published yet).

prices.summary: USD quotes for BTC, ETH and SOL with 24h change. Sources: CoinGecko → CoinPaprika → Binance; served from a 20-second server cache.

fields.name: data[].changePct
fields.desc: 24h change in percent (number, may be 0 when the source omits it)

fields.name: stale
fields.desc: true when all sources failed and this is the last good value

fields.name: updatedAt
fields.desc: ISO-8601 time the value was fetched, or null

sentiment.summary: Crypto Fear & Greed index from Alternative.me; served from a 5-minute server cache. The index itself updates about once a day.

fields.name: data.timestamp
fields.desc: Provider timestamp in milliseconds since epoch

briefs.summary: The most recent published AI Market Brief, detailed tier, in Korean and English. Non-personalized, AI-generated; the aiModel field names the model (or mock-v1 for the template fallback).

fields.name: data.briefDate
fields.desc: YYYY-MM-DD — the calendar date the brief was generated for (UTC date at generation time unless the job passes an explicit date)

fields.name: data.sections
fields.desc: btc, eth, altcoin, macro, today — each an object with ko and en text

fields.name: data.aiModel
fields.desc: Model label shown on the site

limits.title: Rate limit and quota
limits.perMinute: 60 requests per minute per key, counted in a fixed one-minute window.
limits.perMonth: 100,000 calls per calendar month (UTC) across all keys on the account. The usage card above counts the same rows the quota is enforced on.
limits.headers: Every response that passed authentication carries X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining and Retry-After (seconds until the current minute window resets). 401 and 403 responses carry no rate-limit headers.
limits.advice: Cache on your side: prices change at most every 20 s, sentiment every 5 min, briefs once a day. Polling faster than that only spends quota.

errors.shape: Error bodies are a JSON object with a single error string, using the messages above verbatim.

meta.title: The meta field
meta.body: Every response ends with a meta object: provider ("CryptoGuide API v1"), docs (link to this page), disclaimer (ko and en) and terms (ko and en). The data is informational only and not investment advice; redistribution, resale and public re-publication are prohibited. If you store or display the data, keep the disclaimer and terms with it.

webhooks.title: Webhooks
webhooks.body: Register an http(s) URL and we POST to it when a brief or report is published. Up to 5 webhooks per account. Deliveries have a 5-second timeout and are not retried; the last HTTP status is shown next to each webhook. URLs that resolve to private or internal addresses are rejected.
webhooks.events: Events and their data fields: brief.published (briefDate, tier); report.published (slug, locale, cadence, category, periodKey); test.ping (message — sent by the Send test button). The body is always event, data and sentAt.
webhooks.headers: Headers: content-type: application/json, x-cryptoguide-event: <event>, x-cryptoguide-signature: sha256=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body, keyed with your webhook secret>.
webhooks.verify: Verify by recomputing the HMAC over the raw request body and comparing with a constant-time compare. Reject anything that doesn't match; reject old sentAt values if you need replay protection.

versioning.title: Versioning
versioning.body: This is v1. Fields may be added; existing fields are not renamed or removed without a new version prefix.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.subtitle: Answers to the questions we hear most.

q1.question: What is CryptoGuide?
q1.answer: A crypto market information platform with real-time prices, AI news digests, daily market briefings and on-chain data.

q2.question: Do you provide investment advice?
q2.answer: No. CryptoGuide is an informational service and does not provide investment advice, trade solicitation or asset management. All decisions and their consequences are your own responsibility.

q3.question: Is the price data real-time?
q3.answer: We stream public data from global exchanges over WebSocket, updating second by second. Where streaming is blocked (some regions/networks) we fall back to 30-second polling, so slight delays may occur.

q4.question: How do billing and cancellation work?
q4.answer: Paid plans are billed in USD either monthly or yearly (yearly saves about 17%), and can be cancelled anytime. After cancelling, you keep access until the end of the current billing period.

q5.question: Can I change plans later?
q5.answer: Yes. You can upgrade or downgrade anytime, and the difference is applied to your next bill.

q6.question: Do you offer an API?
q6.answer: The API Center is available on the Whale plan, together with data export.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.subtitle: What personal data we process, why, how long we keep it, and your rights.
privacy.intro: The Company values your personal data and complies with applicable data-protection laws, including the Korean Personal Information Protection Act (PIPA) and, where applicable, the GDPR. This policy explains what personal data we collect and use, third-party sharing, retention and your rights.

sections.heading: 1. Personal data we collect
sections.body: Account details (email, name, profile image via Clerk), consent records (timestamp, IP, user-agent), payment data (Stripe customer/subscription identifiers — card data is held by Stripe), portfolios and watchlists, referral relationships and a hashed signup IP, API keys (hashed), service access/usage records, paid-plan waitlist sign-ups (email, plan of interest, language), and enterprise sales inquiries (work email, organization, team size, intended use).

sections.heading: 2. Purposes of use
sections.body: We use personal data for member management and authentication, billing/renewal/refunds of paid subscriptions, providing and improving the Service, meeting legal obligations (such as consent evidence), and preventing abuse (such as referral-fraud detection).

sections.heading: 3. Legal bases
sections.body: We process personal data on the bases permitted by applicable law, including performance of a contract, your consent, legal obligations and legitimate interests.

sections.heading: 4. Sharing and processors
sections.body: To provide the Service we engage processors for authentication (Clerk), payments (Stripe), AI processing (Anthropic), hosting/CDN and email. When AI processing is used, personally identifying data is minimized.

sections.heading: 5. International transfers
sections.body: Some processors are located outside your country; where this occurs we apply the safeguards required by law. The details of international transfers will be finalized and disclosed in the pre-launch legal review.

sections.heading: 6. Retention and deletion
sections.body: Personal data is deleted without undue delay once its purpose is achieved or you close your account, except where a legal retention obligation applies. On account deletion, related data is cascade-deleted.

sections.heading: 7. Your rights
sections.body: You may request access, correction, deletion, restriction and portability of your personal data. You can export your data (portability) and delete your account (erasure) directly from your profile page.

sections.heading: 8. Cookies
sections.body: We use the minimum necessary cookies for keeping you signed in, language preference and referral attribution.

sections.heading: 9. Security
sections.body: We apply technical and organizational measures such as access control, transport encryption and IP hashing to process personal data securely.

sections.heading: 10. Children
sections.body: The Service does not target children below the minimum age set by applicable law and does not knowingly collect their personal data.

disclaimer.subtitle: The nature of the Service and the risks involved.
disclaimer.intro: This Disclaimer clarifies the nature and limits of the CryptoGuide Service. Please read it carefully before using the Service.

sections.heading: 1. Nature of the Service
sections.body: CryptoGuide provides AI-powered market analysis and educational content only. Nothing on this website constitutes financial, investment, tax, or legal advice.

sections.heading: 2. No advisory relationship
sections.body: The Company does not provide investment advisory services and is not registered as an investment adviser in any jurisdiction. Using the Service does not create any advisory, fiduciary or agency relationship between you and the Company.

sections.heading: 3. AI-generated content
sections.body: AI-generated summaries, briefings and pattern analysis are labeled as AI-generated and may be inaccurate. The "confidence" in pattern analysis reflects the degree of shape match, not a prediction of price direction, and briefings are non-personalized information, not tailored to any individual.

sections.heading: 4. Investment risk
sections.body: Trading cryptocurrencies involves substantial risk. You may lose some or all of your capital. You are solely responsible for your own investment decisions and their outcomes.

sections.heading: 5. No guarantee of results
sections.body: Past performance does not guarantee future results. The Company does not guarantee any investment outcome or return.

sections.heading: 6. Third-party data
sections.body: Prices, news and on-chain data in the Service are sourced from third parties, and their accuracy, completeness and timeliness are not guaranteed.

refund.title: Refund Policy
refund.subtitle: How subscription billing, automatic renewal, withdrawal and refunds work.
refund.intro: This Refund Policy governs billing, automatic renewal, withdrawal of subscription and refunds for the paid subscription services provided by CryptoGuide (the "Company"). It forms part of the Company's Terms of Service and does not limit any consumer rights guaranteed by applicable consumer-protection laws, including the Korean Act on the Consumer Protection in Electronic Commerce.

sections.heading: 1. Automatic renewal and advance notice
sections.body: Unless cancelled, every paid subscription renews automatically at the end of each billing cycle and is charged to your registered payment method. The Company sends an email 3 days before the renewal date stating that the subscription will renew and the amount that will be charged.

sections.heading: 2. Free trial
sections.body: New subscriptions include a 7-day free trial. If you cancel during the trial, you are not charged anything. When the trial ends, the subscription automatically converts to a paid subscription and the first charge is made.

sections.heading: 3. Monthly subscriptions
sections.body: Monthly subscriptions are non-refundable. If you cancel, access is not stopped immediately; you may continue to use the service until the end of the current billing period you have already paid for. At the end of the period the subscription ends without renewing.

sections.heading: 4. Annual subscriptions
sections.body: Annual subscriptions are non-refundable as a rule. However, a full refund is available only when the request is made within 14 days of the payment date AND the service has not actually been used (no usage records such as signing in and viewing content). Refunds are not available once 14 days have passed or once there is any record of service use.

sections.heading: 5. Plan changes (upgrade / downgrade)
sections.body: An upgrade to a higher plan takes effect immediately and only the prorated difference for the remaining billing period is charged. A downgrade to a lower plan does not affect the current billing period and applies from the next billing date; no separate refund is provided for a downgrade.

sections.heading: 6. Limits on withdrawal for digital content
sections.body: This service is informational digital content. Under applicable law, including Article 17(2) of the Korean Act on the Consumer Protection in Electronic Commerce, the right to withdraw a subscription may be restricted to the extent permitted by law once provision of the content has begun. Where withdrawal is restricted, the Company clearly indicates this and provides trial use (the free trial) as required by applicable law.

sections.heading: 7. Refunds for cryptocurrency (USDC) payments
sections.body: Where payment was made in cryptocurrency such as USDC, refunds are issued only to the wallet address originally used for the payment. Refunds to a different wallet address are not provided, and network fees at the time of the refund may be deducted. The Company is not responsible for losses caused by the user, such as entering an incorrect wallet address.

refund.how: You can request a refund directly from the subscription management page or through our customer support channel. Eligibility for an annual-subscription refund is determined based on the payment date and service-usage records.

data.title: Data & methodology
data.subtitle: Where our numbers come from, how often they refresh, how the AI text is written, and what can go wrong.
data.intro: CryptoGuide is an information service. Almost everything you see here is pulled from public third-party sources and reassembled — we do not run an exchange, hold funds, or produce a price feed of our own. This page explains, in plain terms, what each feature is built on, how fresh it is, how the automated text is produced, and the limits to keep in mind. It is written to match the code that actually runs; when we change a source or a schedule, we update this page.

sources.title: Where the data comes from
sources.intro: Each feature reads from one or more public sources, in a fixed order. If the first source fails or rate-limits us, we try the next one.

items.heading: Crypto prices (dashboard, ticker, watchlist, portfolio)
items.body: USD prices for BTC, ETH and SOL on the dashboard, and for the 8-coin ticker (BTC, ETH, SOL, BNB, XRP, ADA, DOGE, AVAX), come from CoinGecko first, then CoinPaprika, then Binance. While your browser can reach Binance, the ticker also streams live updates over Binance's public WebSocket; where it can't (from US networks, for example), the ticker falls back to polling our snapshot every 30 seconds. Watchlist and portfolio valuations use Binance USDT spot prices with CoinPaprika as the fallback; when several coins share a ticker symbol, the highest-ranked one wins.

items.heading: Global markets
items.body: NASDAQ, S&P 500, KOSPI, gold, WTI crude and the US Dollar Index come from the Yahoo Finance chart endpoint, with a mirror host as fallback. The daily change is the current price against the previous close.

items.heading: Fear & Greed
items.body: The crypto Fear & Greed index is the one published by Alternative.me; we show its value and classification unchanged. The provider updates the index about once a day.

items.heading: News
items.body: Headlines are collected from six RSS feeds, balanced across regions: CoinDesk and Cointelegraph (US), BeInCrypto and CryptoNews (Europe), AMBCrypto and TokenPost (Asia). We take at most 8 items per source per run so no single outlet dominates, de-duplicate by link, and store the headline, link, source and publish time. The summary under each headline is written by us automatically (see “How the AI text is produced”). The “market sentiment (news tone)” gauge aggregates the per-article tone over the last 24 hours — it reflects how headlines read, not where the market is going.

items.heading: Chart patterns
items.body: Pattern and support/resistance detection runs on Binance candle (OHLC) data, 200 candles per symbol and interval. The detection itself is a set of fixed geometric rules, not an AI model. The confidence score measures how well the candles fit the shape; it says nothing about where price goes next.

items.heading: On-chain
items.body: The whale tracker lists recent Bitcoin transactions of $5M or more from Blockchair (the 15 most recent), falling back to the largest transactions in blockchain.info's unconfirmed-transaction sample when Blockchair is unavailable. Exchange inflow/outflow is an estimate: we take that sample and match inputs and outputs against a public list of known exchange wallets, so it reflects a sample, not total flows. Network activity (active addresses, transactions, hash rate, miner revenue, 30 days) comes from blockchain.info charts; stablecoin supply (USDT, USDC and DAI market caps) comes from CoinGecko.

items.heading: Crypto Map
items.body: Merchants and ATMs come from BTCMap, which is built on OpenStreetMap data contributed by volunteers. We import the location, name, address, category and payment tags (on-chain / Lightning); where an entry has no explicit payment tag we assume Bitcoin. The list of online services and the per-country regulation status are curated by us (see the map notes below).

items.heading: AI brief and reports
items.body: The daily brief and the weekly, monthly and quarterly reports are written from the inputs above: the current BTC/ETH/SOL quotes, the Fear & Greed reading, the last 24 hours of published headlines and, for reports, the on-chain series. Nothing else goes in.

cadence.title: How often things refresh
cadence.intro: Two things matter: how often we ask the source, and how often your screen asks us. The figures below are the ones in the code.

rows.cadence: Server keeps a quote for 20 seconds; the page refetches every 30 seconds.
Real-time over WebSocket where Binance is reachable from your browser; otherwise our snapshot, refreshed every 15 seconds on the server and polled every 30 seconds by the page.
Server keeps the price list for 15 seconds.
Checked every 5 minutes; the index itself changes about once a day.
New headlines are collected every 30 minutes; summaries are written in the same run (up to 20 per run), with a follow-up job for anything left over.
Once a day, in the morning (Korea Standard Time), in a standard and a detailed version.
Server keeps the list for 60 seconds.
Conditions are evaluated about once a minute, so an alert normally arrives within a few minutes of the event — not second by second.
Merchant and ATM data is synced from BTCMap about once a day (only entries changed since the last sync). Regulation status changes when we edit it.

resilience.title: What happens when a source is down
resilience.body: Every market call has a short timeout and one retry. If a source answers with a rate limit, we leave it alone for 60 seconds and move on to the next one. If every source fails, we show the last value we did get and mark it stale (the API returns stale: true; the dashboard keeps the last value on screen). We never fill a gap with an invented number — if we have never received a value, the section simply stays empty until we do.

ai.title: How the AI text is produced
ai.intro: News summaries, the daily market brief, research reports and the portfolio commentary are written automatically by a large language model (Anthropic's Claude when configured). The model only sees the inputs listed above — it has no web access and no memory of you — and every piece of generated text is labeled with the model that produced it.
rules: It must be grounded in the data and headlines it was given. No invented facts, numbers or events.
No definitive predictions. It may say a move “could” or “appears to” be happening; it may not say that a price will reach a level.
No instructions to buy, sell, enter, exit or rebalance, and no entry, target or stop levels.

Non-personalized: the brief and reports are generated once and shown identically to everyone. Portfolio commentary explains diversification metrics only — the model receives percentages and index values, never amounts, holdings tied to you, or identifiers — and is discarded after it is shown.
ai.checks: Before anything is published, the output goes through automatic checks: length, formatting artifacts, and a list of banned phrases in Korean and English (definitive predictions, trade directives, profit guarantees). If a check fails we retry once; if it still fails the item is held back and shown as “withheld” rather than published. There is also a daily cap on model calls; when it is reached, pending items wait for the next day.
ai.fallback: Summaries and briefs are generated automatically. When the language model is not available, a rule-based template fallback writes the text from the same numbers and headlines, and the AI label shows “mock-v1” instead of a model name. Treat these the same way as any other automated text: a starting point for your own reading, not a conclusion.
ai.notAdvice: None of this is a recommendation. The tone is deliberately descriptive; if a sentence reads like advice, that is a bug and we would like to hear about it.

items.heading: Delays
items.body: Prices can be up to about 30 seconds behind the market, global market quotes up to a minute, news up to 30 minutes, and the Fear & Greed index a day. Nothing here is suitable for timing trades.

items.heading: Third-party accuracy
items.body: We pass sources through; we do not audit them. An error upstream — a bad print, a mis-tagged merchant, a stale RSS item — will appear here too.

items.heading: Coverage
items.body: The dashboard tracks 3 coins and the ticker 8; the watchlist and portfolio support whatever Binance or CoinPaprika lists. Global markets are 6 instruments. News is 6 English- and Korean-language outlets. The map shows what BTCMap contributors have mapped, which in many regions is a fraction of the places that actually accept crypto.

items.heading: Regional differences
items.body: Binance is unreachable from some networks (the US, for example). There the ticker polls instead of streaming, and chart patterns may show “candle data unavailable” until another source is added.

items.heading: Symbol collisions
items.body: Many coins share a ticker symbol. For watchlist and portfolio prices we resolve a symbol to the highest-ranked coin with that ticker — usually, but not always, the one you mean.

items.heading: Estimates
items.body: Exchange inflow/outflow is computed from a sample of unconfirmed transactions matched against a public wallet list; actual totals differ. Pattern confidence is a shape score, not a probability.

items.heading: AI text
items.body: Even when grounded and checked, model output can misread a headline, over-weight a detail, or phrase things awkwardly. Held items are not shown; published items can still be wrong. The template fallback is a further step down in nuance.

items.heading: Availability
items.body: Scheduled jobs (news, brief, map sync, alerts) can run late. When they do, the timestamps on each page tell you how old the data is.

map.title: Crypto Map: extra notes
items: Merchant data is community-maintained. A pin means someone added the place to OpenStreetMap/BTCMap and said it accepts Bitcoin — not that we checked. Places close, stop accepting crypto, or move. Where a “verified” date is shown, that is the last survey date recorded by contributors.
From the map data we show Bitcoin on-chain and Lightning acceptance only; coins listed for online services come from our own curated list.

Country regulation status is our summary, in five coarse labels (friendly / regulated / restricted / banned / unclear), for a limited set of countries, and is edited by hand. It is a starting point for reading, not legal advice: rules differ inside a country, change often, and our label may lag a change by weeks or more.
The map does not broker, verify or guarantee any transaction, and we are not a party to anything you do at a listed place.

retention.title: What we store about you
retention.intro: The full version is the Privacy Policy; this is the short, practical list based on what the database actually holds.

items.heading: Account
items.body: Email, name and profile image (managed by Clerk), plus your language, time zone and country code.

items.heading: Consent records
items.body: Which document version you agreed to, when, and the IP address and browser string at that moment — kept as evidence of consent.

items.heading: Subscription
items.body: Stripe customer and subscription identifiers. Card details never touch our servers.

items.heading: Your content
items.body: Portfolios and holdings, watchlists, saved articles and reports, notifications, alert rules, alert channel settings (a Telegram chat ID or email address you give us) and delivery history.

items.heading: Referral
items.body: Your referral code, who referred whom, and a salted hash of the signup IP (the raw address is not kept).

items.heading: API (Whale plan)
items.body: A hash and a short prefix of each API key (the full key is shown once and not stored), per-day call counts per key and endpoint, and webhook URLs and secrets.

items.heading: Usage signal
items.body: One row per hour per feature noting that you used the service — kept to determine refund eligibility, not for analytics.

items.heading: Security log
items.body: Account deletion, data export, admin actions and blocked requests, with IP and browser string. This log is append-only and survives account deletion: the link to your user record is removed, but the entry keeps the acting email address.

items.heading: Forms
items.body: Paid-plan waitlist sign-ups (email, plan, language) and enterprise inquiries (work email, organization, team size, intended use).

items.heading: Product events
items.body: Lightweight events (event name, page, locale) used to understand which features are used.

notStored: Raw signup IP addresses (only a salted hash).
Portfolio AI commentary (generated on request, returned, discarded).
Full API keys or the contents of webhook deliveries.
retention.controls: From your profile you can export everything stored on your account as JSON and delete the account. Deletion cascades to all of the above except the security log.

corrections.title: Corrections and questions
corrections.body: If a number looks wrong, a merchant pin is out of date, a regulation label is behind, or an AI sentence reads like advice, tell us. Include the page, roughly when you saw it and, if you can, a screenshot. We fix what is ours and report upstream what isn't.
corrections.mapTip: For merchant pins, the fastest route is often to fix the entry on BTCMap/OpenStreetMap directly; we pick the change up on the next sync.
